## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

::: notes
```{=html}
CDE with the help of many others, such as the staff at the Center for Assessment, have developed a great, user friendly tool that provides districts and principals now, <br>
And hopefully teachers in the near future, with a visual map of both their overall performance compared to schools in their district, as well as building level exploration <br>
Capabilities.<br>
<br>
On the splash page they have introductory tutorials about what the growth model is and how to use the interface.
```

Here I have selected to view all the 5th graders in my building. From here I can <br>

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

::: notes
```{=html}
Bethanne, scored on the cusp of the partially proficient and unsatisfactory categories in 3rd grade. But dropped in to unsat by 4th.<br>
<br>
From here we want to know two things: how much growth did Bethanne achieve and how much did she need to move up (rather than down)?
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

::: notes
```{=html}
Here we see that her growth was low between 3rd and 4th grade and between 4th and 5th.<br>
<br>
Had she grown in the typical range (growth of 35 to 64th percentile) she would have been pp. <br>
<br>
Now we need to ask: how much growth does she need to move up next year?
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

::: notes
```{=html}
We see here that she need to grow in the high growth range (65th-99th percentile) in order to move up to proficiency.<br>
<br>
Since she has historically grown in the low growth range, what needs to be done?<br>
<br>
Now what about other subjects?
```
:::

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/10.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

::: notes
```{=html}
She is doing better in reading, but has slipped in the last year.<br>
<br>
You can see that this info can be used to put this student on an RtI plan.<br>
<br>
Because the interface is so visual data teams, or all 6th grade teachers (in this example) and relatively quickly go through individual students<br>
At the beginning of each year—using this info to assign students to classrooms or programs, cluster kids by strengths and needs, etc<br>
<br>
Now lets look at pattern identification
```
:::

::: notes
```{=html}
2. With regard to your answer to question 1: How/where do local data (e.g., interim assessments, classroom observations) fit in?<br>
 In this model, the data is the result at the end of the year, which teachers do not see until the beginning of the next year.<br>
 Interim assessment and classroom observations, therefore, have two uses<br>
 1st they inform the teacher about a students progress during the course of the academic year, when there is still time for intervention.<br>
 2nd they can be used in conjunction with the year end measures to assess the effectiveness of the teacher’s/school’s curriculum/practices with last years students<br>
 in order to make corrections, adjustments to plans for this years students (based on their formative and summative data)<br>
 <br>
The League is developing our trainings to help schools do this well and I know Rebecca, in Arizona, has already done to do work around this…
```
:::
